## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymous. The guidelines say that to ensure a double-anonymous process authors must remove identifying information from submitted materials except the title page (guidelines copy 2026-02-01), and the publish-with-us page says the same (copy 2025-04-23). Self-citations are to be written in the third person, and the preregistration of a preregistered study must not carry author information (guidelines copy 2026-02-01) |
| **Process** | A manuscript judged by the co-editors-in-chief to be of sufficient quality and in line with the mission is assigned to one of the editors-in-chief, who acts as action editor or hands it to an associate editor; the action editor secures reviewers and judges publication worthiness from reviewer feedback and their own reading; the editors-in-chief send the final decision letter (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer statement found in the guidelines copy |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found in the guidelines copy (searched for open review wording: none) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev: 1.5 review rounds on average, 3.0 review reports on average (2 reviews; https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-communication/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal itself states no figure |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | The journal's decision wording is not published in the guidelines copy. It says that an invitation to revise and resubmit may come with a request for supplemental items listed in the decision letter (guidelines copy 2026-02-01) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, in part. The live guidelines read in a real browser 2026-11-24 (https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/General_Instructions) require an "AI Use Declaration" (with a Data Availability Statement and a Conflict of Interest Statement) on the title page, and a section "Disclosure of AI use" says authors must follow OUP's central Policy on AI Use & Disclosure for OUP Journals Authors and "also follow the Journal's specific policy variations"; no variation is spelled out on that page. The supplemental-materials list suggests a "compendium of prompts" used with large language models or chatbots. The Wayback copy of 2026-02-01 had none of this text. The page also says submissions may be screened with third-party services for integrity issues such as image alteration and paper-mill activity. The sister journal's guidelines say authors "should review" the ICA Publications Committee's generative-AI guidelines for all ICA publications and should disclose any AI use in the research process in the cover letter, with some uses also going in the Methods or other sections (JCMC guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions). The ICA recommendation itself (https://cdn.ymaws.com/www.icahdq.org/resource/resmgr/docs/AI_Pub_Comm_Recomendations.pdf, undated one page, retrieved 2026-11-23) says authors should not list AI software as an author and that content or analysis generated by a generative AI tool at any point in the research workflow must be noted in the Methods (or Acknowledgments, if there is no Methods section) at submission. Whether the journal applies it to submissions is not stated on the JoC page copy; the PDF adds that editorial decisions on AI use are made by each journal's editorial team. The OUP policy page was read in a real browser 2026-11-24 (see Summary) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No permission gate; a mandatory AI Use Declaration on the title page, and for uses that need disclosure the OUP policy asks for it in the cover letter and Acknowledgements (live guidelines and OUP policy, 2026-11-24) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 4 (this entry's own reading): language polishing and reference formatting need no disclosure; editing, translation, data work, code and illustrative images are allowed with disclosure; presenting AI output as human research data is not allowed (OUP journals policy). A declaration is compulsory at submission |
| **Summary** | AI Use Declaration required on the title page; OUP journals policy dated 13 July 2026 (read 2026-11-24): disclose in the cover letter and Acknowledgements (Methods too where AI was integral), at submission and on revision, with tool name and version, how it was used and the author's role in checking it; failure to disclose may be grounds for rejection. ICA Publications Committee recommendation (described as for all ICA publications; the live JoC page does not link it): no AI authorship; AI-generated content or analysis noted in the Methods or Acknowledgments |
| **Source URL** | https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/General_Instructions ; https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/ai-principles-for-oxford-journals/policy-on-ai-use-and-disclosure-for-oxford-journals-authors ; https://cdn.ymaws.com/www.icahdq.org/resource/resmgr/docs/AI_Pub_Comm_Recomendations.pdf (ICA recommendation) |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy plus the journal's own preprint sentence. Sources: https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b (OUP author self-archiving policy, snapshot 2026-11-02) and the guidelines copy of 2026-02-01.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The guidelines say authors keep the right to make an Author's Original Version available through various channels and that this does not prevent submission. The OUP policy lets authors post it anywhere at any time (including commercial platforms and social media) provided that, once accepted, they add a short acknowledgment that it was accepted by the journal |
| Under review | Not separately stated | The OUP definition covers the un-refereed version completed before submission; neither the policy nor the guidelines address the under-review stage on its own. Double-anonymous review depends on authors not exposing identity (see Peer Review) |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | Per OUP policy the accepted manuscript may go on the author's personal webpage immediately and in non-commercial repositories after an embargo; "embargo periods may vary between journals". The OUP embargo list (https://academic.oup.com/pages/open-research/open-access/charges-licences-and-self-archiving/accepted-manuscript-embargo-periods, read in a real browser 2026-11-24) gives "12 months" for Journal of Communication. Embargo: 12 months |
| Version of Record | Restricted | Not to be deposited in repositories unless published open access (OUP policy copy 2026-11-02); sharing in private groups is allowed in the cases the policy lists |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the live guidelines page, read in a real browser 2026-11-24 (https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/General_Instructions). The earlier Wayback copy of 2026-02-01 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions) gave a 35-page limit instead of the word limit below; where this table says "guidelines copy" elsewhere in the entry, the live page is the authority.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original research articles and book reviews (the mission statement), plus invited responses (unsolicited response submissions are asked not to be sent) and the JoC Forum, which takes review essays of three or more books, 3,000 to 6,000 words, and is peer reviewed; authors are asked to contact the Forum editors before submitting. OpenAlex type counts for 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 245 articles, 19 book reviews, 11 reviews, 8 errata, 3 editorials (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | Live page: the main document is "a maximum of 8000 words (including the abstract, main text, references, tables, figures, and endnotes)", in 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, 1.0 inch margins. The 2026-02-01 Wayback copy gave a 35-page limit and no word limit; the live page no longer states a page limit. Forum pieces: 3,000 to 6,000 words |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No statement on exceptions to the 8000-word limit |
| **Abstract limit** | Maximum 150 words, and at least 5 keywords of the author's choosing, on page 1 (with the title) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 8000 words. APA 7th edition; references start on a new page |
| **Supplementary material** | A single supplemental-materials document is allowed and does not count against the main-document limit (instruments, stimuli, codebooks, code, interview guides and similar); none is required at first submission, and editors may request items at revise-and-resubmit |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables and figures go after the references, one per page (at most two simple ones per page); alt text for figures is requested |
| **Style / submission format** | APA 7th edition (the live page says submissions that do not comply with the style requirements "will be immediately rejected", as it does for non-anonymised ones); a cap of one original article every 6 months per corresponding author, with over-limit submissions rejected; a cover-letter explanation of how a paper differs from others on the same primary data set; preregistration not required, but if done the cover letter must document it; Word file only (the page says PDF is not accepted); one main document, an optional supplemental document and a title page with contact details and a short biographical statement per author, submitted online via the journal's submission site; effect sizes should be supplied where appropriate; the APA's bias-free language guidance is asked for |

### Orientation

> Counts below come from Crossref journal-article records for 2021-01 to 2026-11-23: 287 records, of which 235 (81.9%) carry an abstract; a record is counted when the pattern matches in its title or abstract; shares use the 235 as the denominator, so counts are lower bounds for the 52 records without an abstract (https://api.crossref.org/journals/1460-2466/works, cursor paging, retrieved 2026-11-23). Every regex is given in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics. The first-pass tool `topic_trend_scan.py` was not used (known broken).

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword: experiment-type words in 49 of 235 abstracts (20.9%), survey-type words in 42 (17.9%); a broad conceptual/theoretical pattern matches 41 (17.4%) but that pattern also matches empirical abstracts that name a theory, so it is not a count of purely theoretical papers |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Quantitative designs are more frequent: interview-type words in 26 (11.1%) and qualitative-method words in 21 (8.9%) against the experiment and survey counts above. The journal says all methods are welcome ("All theoretical approaches as well as methods of scholarly inquiry are welcome", guidelines copy 2026-02-01) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The guidelines say manuscripts should be relevant "to scholars across specializations" and the journal is especially interested in work that connects threads across subfields (guidelines copy 2026-02-01). Board members' institutions are listed without department, so disciplines could not be counted |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope condition is stated: manuscripts are expected to make original contributions to communication research and to "address critical theoretical and empirical questions in communication that are relevant to scholars across specializations" (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions).
- **What kind of engagement?** The journal is "particularly interested" in manuscripts that connect analytical threads across communication subfields or make major theoretical contributions of relevance beyond one area; arguments are expected to be theoretically sophisticated, conceptually meaningful and methodologically sound (same page). The about page copy of 2025-08-21 says the journal is especially interested in work whose significance crosses disciplinary and subfield boundaries (https://web.archive.org/web/20250821023308/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/About).
- **Article type and length**: original articles up to 8000 words including abstract, references, tables, figures and endnotes (live guidelines 2026-11-24; the Wayback copy had a 35-page limit); abstract up to 150 words; at least 5 keywords; Forum review essays 3,000 to 6,000 words (guidelines copy 2026-02-01). The guidelines point to an editorial by the current editors-in-chief on the journal's vision and the manuscripts sought (title: "Navigating the Seas of Inclusivity: A Collaborative Voyage at the Helm of a Communication Flagship Journal"; the editorial text itself was not read).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the guidelines say submissions that closely resemble previously published articles by the same authors "will be immediately rejected", and the process summary says the editors-in-chief first screen for quality and fit with the mission (guidelines copy 2026-02-01). No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions beyond that; SciRev shows 2 reviews and no desk-rejection data (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-communication/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: Crossref journal-article records 2021-01 to 2026-11-23, 287 records, 235 with an abstract; a hit is a match in title or abstract; share = hits / 235. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The only editorial statement found is the general "all methods welcome" sentence (guidelines copy 2026-02-01), which does not favour one method, so no row is scored 4 or 5. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. All patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `\b(experiment\w*\|randomi[sz]ed\|between-subjects?\|within-subjects?)\b` 49 of 235 (20.9%); title-only 7 of 287. Survey pattern `\b(surveys?\|questionnaires?\|self-report\w*\|panel (?:survey\|data\|study))\b` 42 (17.9%). Preregistration pattern `\bpre-?regist\w*` 12 (5.1%); the journal says it does "not require" preregistration (guidelines copy 2026-02-01) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `\b(interview\w*\|semi-structured\|focus groups?)\b` 26 of 235 (11.1%); broader qualitative pattern `\b(qualitative\|thematic analysis\|ethnograph\w*\|discourse analysis\|grounded theory)\b` 21 (8.9%); title-only 12 of 287 |
| Autoethnography | 0 | `\bautoethnograph\w*` 0 of 235 abstracts and 0 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\b(conceptual\w*\|theori[sz]\w*)\b` 41 of 235 (17.4%); the pattern also matches empirical abstracts that mention a theory, so it overstates purely theoretical work; title-only 4 of 287 |
| Mixed methods | 2 | `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b` 4 of 235 (1.7%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 3 | `\b(meta-analy\w*\|systematic review\w*\|meta-synthesis\|scoping review)\b` 12 of 235 (5.1%); title-only 12 of 287 (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1093/joc/jqad024) |
| Computational / digital-trace methods (added row) | 3 | `\b(computational\|machine learning\|topic model\w*\|natural language processing\|large language models?\|web tracking\|digital trace\w*)\b` 14 of 235 (6.0%); content-analysis pattern `\bcontent analys[ie]s\b` 7 (3.0%) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Sample (abstract-only text; titles and full texts not searched): in Crossref abstracts, 172 of 235 (73.2%) contain a first-person word (pattern `\b(?:I\|[Ww]e\|[Mm]y\|[Oo]ur)\b`, case-sensitive; plural "we" may be generic or authorial); among the 10 most recent abstracts by publication date, 6 contain one (DOIs 10.1093/joc/jqag024, jqag023, jqag021, jqag014, jqag016, jqag013 contain it; jqag020, jqag017, jqag018, jqag015 do not). Abstracts only: full texts are paywalled, and the guidelines give no first-person rule |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 35 double-spaced pages including references, tables and figures (guidelines copy 2026-02-01); the journal states no word count for articles. Crossref author lists for 282 of 287 records: 1 author 73, 2 authors 61, 3 authors 55, 4 or more 93 (includes forum and review items) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Maximum 150 words; at least 5 keywords chosen by the author; abstract and title on page 1 (guidelines copy 2026-02-01) |
| **Writing style notes** | APA 7th edition for text and references; second-order headings bold and flush left; the title serves as the first-order heading for the introduction; self-citation written in the third person ("Xi and Smith (2024) have demonstrated" is the page's own example); effect sizes expected where appropriate; APA bias-free and inclusive language (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions) |
| **Authorship pattern** | See the Crossref author-count line above; 73 of 282 records with author lists have one author (26%), but the denominator includes non-research items |

Disciplines are not listed | https://web.archive.org/web/20250820232156/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/Editorial_Board |

The action editor "secures reviewers" per the process summary, so reviewers are not limited to the board | Guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Required in the manuscript. The live Publication Ethics paragraph (read in a real browser 2026-11-24) says details of approval by the author's Institutional Review Board or similar oversight body should be included in the manuscript, with the institution anonymised at submission; where the institution has no such process, authors should give a critical reflection on ethical risks and the steps taken to reduce them. COPE standards apply; falsification, fabrication, plagiarism and duplicate publication of one's own work are unacceptable. (The 2026-02-01 Wayback copy had no wording on institutional review) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author items exist: 73 of 282 Crossref records with author lists (2021-2026; includes forum and review items) have one author; research articles alone were not separated |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No rule found: the title page asks for contact details and a short biographical statement per author (guidelines copy 2026-02-01); the page text read has no affiliation requirement or independent-scholar clause. The publish-with-us page said ICA members "can submit an unlimited number of papers" (copy 2025-04-23), but the live guidelines (2026-11-24) cap every author at one original article per 6 months as corresponding author, with no membership exception stated |
| **Data transparency requirement** | A Data Availability Statement is a requirement for published articles, under the heading "Data availability"; the journal "strongly encourages" making data available where ethically feasible; datasets must be cited with a persistent identifier; voluntary Open Science Badges (open materials, open data, preregistered) are offered (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymous review: identifying information removed from main and supplemental documents, self-citation in the third person, preregistration free of author information; the title page is retained by the editors (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions). Author's Original Version may be posted anywhere before acceptance (OUP policy copy 2026-11-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b), which would expose identity; whether the journal treats a posted preprint as a problem for anonymity is not stated |
| **AI use** | AI Use Declaration required on the title page; OUP journals disclosure policy applies (see AI Policy) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; OpenAlex lists an APC of 4235 USD (not confirmed: the publisher's charge form could not be used); society-membership discount exists, amount unread (see Open Access) |
| **Originality screening** | The guidelines state manuscripts "may also be screened" with third-party services for integrity issues such as image alteration and paper-mill activity (guidelines copy 2026-02-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212514/https://academic.oup.com/joc/pages/general_instructions); a similarity-check service is not named |

**Method notes:** In table cells the alternation bar of each regex is written `\|` so the markdown table does not break; the regex itself uses a plain `|`. Crossref was fetched with cursor paging (rows 200) filtered to ISSN 1460-2466 and 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23; 287 journal-article records. Patterns are Python `re` with the case flag stated; matches run over lower- or mixed-case title plus abstract with HTML tags removed. The Crossref abstract field begins with the word "Abstract", which does not affect these patterns. OpenAlex was used for four count queries and the source record (one request every 2.2 seconds, no key, no 429). Board countries were assigned from institution names by a lookup table written for this pass; ambiguous cases were Hong Kong and Macau (kept separate) and the page's two spellings of Buffalo and of Hebrew University (each person counted once).

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: the main document may not exceed 8000 words including abstract, references, tables, figures and endnotes (Format; live guidelines 2026-11-24). A longer manuscript departs from a stated rule; whether exceptions are granted is not stated.
- **Submission cap and style**: one original article per 6 months as corresponding author, and non-compliance with APA style or anonymisation is a stated ground for immediate rejection (Format).
- **Anonymisation**: the journal uses double-anonymous review and asks for removal of identifying information, third-person self-citation and author-free preregistrations (Peer Review). A manuscript that cannot be anonymised does not meet the stated submission rules.
- **File format**: Word only, no PDF (Format; guidelines copy 2026-02-01).
- **Data availability statement**: required for published articles (Practical Concerns), so a paper with no statable position on data access cannot meet that requirement.
- Other stated requirements: an AI Use Declaration, a Data Availability Statement and a Conflict of Interest Statement on the title page, and IRB approval details in the manuscript (AI Policy, Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the guidelines say decisions on initial submissions usually come within 90 days (Review Cycle Time); SciRev reports 2.2 months for a first round and 3.3 months for handling accepted manuscripts (n=2, anecdote).
- **Open access cost**: gold OA is paid; OpenAlex lists 4235 USD, not confirmed by the publisher (Open Access). Green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to a 12-month embargo (Preprint Policy).
- **Reporting burden**: effect sizes expected, a data availability statement required, and an optional supplemental document with instruments and code is invited and may be requested at revision (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Preprint and anonymity**: posting a preprint is allowed by the publisher but would expose identity under double-anonymous review (Preprint Policy, OPSEC compatibility).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical communication research using experiments, surveys or computational methods, where such designs appear in 49, 42 and 14 of 235 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Work whose point reaches beyond one subfield, which the journal states it prefers (Framing Requirements).
- Topics with regular coverage: news and journalism (53 of 235), social media (37), political polarization (28), misinformation (13) and AI/algorithms (13) (Epistemological & Political Leanings, Sensitive Topics).
- Authors who can supply open materials and data statements, since the journal runs open-science badges and requires a data statement (Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Autoethnography: 0 of 235 abstracts and 0 titles match (Methodological Preferences). This shows absence, not rejection.
- Authors needing a verified turnaround or acceptance figure: the journal publishes none, and SciRev has 2 reviews (Review Cycle Time, Metrics).
- Manuscripts that need more than 8000 words including references, tables and endnotes (Format).
- Authors who cannot make an AI declaration or who submit often: a declaration is compulsory and each corresponding author may submit one original article per 6 months (AI Policy, Format).
